Medipelli Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana on 17 November,
2023
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.31777 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: Medipelli Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The present writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:-
"...to pass an order or orders one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus to declare the illegal action of the Respondent No.4 in harassing the Petitioner by summoning the Petitioner to the Chilpur Police Station and insisting for the settlement in Civil Case and threatening the Petitioner by blackmailing the petitioner to settle and already settled issue and also direct the respondent Nos. 2 to 3 to provide police protection as there is a threat to the petitioner's life from Respondent No.4 which is guaranteed the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the Respondent Nos. 2 to 3 not to harass the Petitioner by Summoning the Petitioner to the Chilpur Police Station and not to involve in civil cases with regard to any civil dispute or settlement between petitioner and Respondent No.4..."
2. The case of the petitioner is that without registering any case he was summoned by respondent Nos.2 and 3 to the police and confined him in the police station for hours together.

The grievance of the petitioner is that at the CVBR, J Wp_31777_2023 instance of respondent No.4, respondent Nos.2 and 3 are interfering with the civil disputes pending between him and respondent No.4 and forcing him to enter into a settlement with respondent No.4 as per the terms dictated by him.

3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 has submitted that respondent No.4 had lodged a complaint against the petitioner and as the said complaint revealed cognizable offence a case in Crime No.214 of 2023 was registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of I.P.C. and for the purpose of investigation the petitioner was summoned to the police.

It is further submitted by the learned Assistant Government Pleader that the respondents-police will follow the procedure contemplated under the provisions of the Cr.P.C. if the presence of the petitioner is required for the purpose of investigation in the above crime.

4. In view of the said submissions, this Court, deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition,
directing respondent No.3 to follow the procedure contemplated under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C. and the guidelines issued by CVBR, J Wp_31777_2023 the Hon'ble Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs.
State of Bihar 1 if the presence of the petitioner is required for the purpose of investigation in Crime No.214 of 2023.
5.

State of Bihar

sentences.text: With the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
